summary: Ryūshō Hikata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu (~1914–1917). He held a professorship at Kyushu University (~1928–1958) and later served at Fukuoka Women's University (~1958–1969).
Ryūō Asahi worked in Buddhist studies. He held teaching posts at Koyasan University and at Toji.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Madras (~1890–1897). He later held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras (~1914–1929).

S. Kuppuswami Sastri was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He was a professor at Presidency University, Kolkata, Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency College, Chennai (~1914–1935), and later Dean and Honorary Professor at Annamalai University (~1935–1943).

S. N. Balagangadhara studied at Ghent University (~1978–1987) in the fields of philosophy and religious studies. He served as Professor in Comparative Science of Cultures and director of its research centre at Ghent University (~1991–2018).
S. N. Savadi was an Indology scholar who held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, attested in 1953 and 1969.

S. S. Suryanarayana Sastri was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He served at the University of Madras, where he was attested as Reader in Indian Philosophy in 1929 and as Reader and Head of the Department of Philosophy in 1942.

S. Sankaranarayanan was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He served as an Honorary Professor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and held a post at the Chinmaya International Foundation in 1999.

Sabine Löhr, an Indology scholar, studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing doctoral work under Lambert Schmithausen. She also served as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at the University of Hamburg.

Sadahiko Kariya worked in Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (attested 1977) and as a professor in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies at Chizan Senmon Gakko (attested 2001).

Sadajiro Sugiura was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied at Rikkyo University (~1889–1893) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1895–1898). He later held a post at Rikkyo University.
Saileswar Sen was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta until 1920 and completed doctoral studies under Barend Faddegon.
Sakda Hemthep studied Buddhist studies and religious studies at Cardiff University, earning a Master of Philosophy under supervisor Max Deeg in 2014.
Sakya Trizin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Appey, Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, and the 14th Dalai Lama, Tenzin Gyatso.

Sakyong Mipham is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Khenpo Namdrol, Penor Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1987–1991). He eventually succeeded Chögyam Trungpa.

Sallie B. King studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (~1972–1974). Working in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, she became Professor (~1991) and later Professor Emerita of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University.

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman studied at UC Berkeley (PhD 1979) under research supervisor Shivaram Dattatray Joshi and traditional teacher T. Shrinivas Shastri. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, she held an attested post at UC Berkeley in 1996.
Sally McAra is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. She completed an MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000) under the supervision of Christine Dureau and Karen Nero.
Sally Mellick Cutler, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, earned her D.Phil. at the University of Oxford in 1993. She served as manager of the Pali Text Society Office, attested in 1997.

Salomon Lefmann was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp (~1858–1864). He later served in the Sanskrit Extraordinariat at Heidelberg University (~1870–1907).
